messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate detected on decode-stream pool (srv-decode-*) — 14 OOM crashes in last 5m. Paging primary on-call Ashok (oncall). Impact: increased 5xxs, client timeouts. :rotating_light:

Ashok (oncall): seeing the page — Pulling logs now. Is this affecting hosted and dedicated?

Jules (support): Customer reports: multiple dropped streaming responses, some requests never returned. Affected customers on hosted tier only so far. Escalating to runtime.

Maria (eng-runtime): I can join — checking node logs and recent deploys. Any recent model or config change to streaming defaults?

Ashok (oncall): not seeing deploys in the last 30m. Quick grep on pods: `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep decode` shows a few crashlooping.

ops-bot: Recent autoscaler activity: increased decode pool by 3 nodes at 1794300900 due to burst.

Sam (sre): grabbing stack traces. Attaching recent container stderr snippet:

```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 23.56 GiB total capacity; 21.10 GiB already allocated; 512 MiB free; 18 allocations from this process)
  at ./aten/src/THC/THCStorage.cpp:xx
  at decode_loop.cpp:decode_step
  at server/stream_handler.cpp:process_chunk
```

Maria (eng-runtime): That looks like a classic streaming decode runaway — `max_tokens` enforcement didn't trigger. I'm seeing repeated requests with `max_tokens: 50000` (client-side misconfig). The streaming path wasn't limiting allocations per-step because of older guardrail PR not applied to the streaming handler.

Ashok (oncall): Oof. So a client sent an enormous `max_tokens`. Is it malformed or abused? Jules any customer context?

Jules (support): One of the affected customers is in PLG onboarding — their integration tested with `max_tokens: 100000` in a dev script. Might be user mistake. We should still mitigate to protect infra.

Maria (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigation options:
- apply a runtime patch to enforce per-request token ceiling in streaming path (low-latency but needs a hotfix)
- temporarily block streaming on decode pool via routing rule
- scale up and sacrifice latency (temporary)
- kill specific runaway pods (manual)

Ashok (oncall): Priorities: protect other customers (avoid noisy neighbor), keep lowest disruption. Suggest we route streaming requests from hosted customer tier to fallback slower model that has stricter token limits, and flip a rate-limit rule to reject >5k tokens. Can we do that quickly?

Maria (eng-runtime): Yes — we can flip a routing policy to send new streaming requests to `model-legacy-small` which has a per-request hard cap, and keep decode pool in read-only mode to drain existing sessions. Doing a canary route first. I'll open the route change: `rbctl route set --from streaming --to model-legacy-small --match tier==hosted --dry-run=false`

ops-bot: route change applied by Maria at 1794301302 — new route will affect new sessions in ~10s.

Sam (sre): I'll cordon the worst nodes and restart pods after we drain. Which nodes? Listing worst offenders: `srv-decode-12`, `srv-decode-14`, `srv-decode-09` with repeated OOMs.

Maria (eng-runtime): Starting a targeted restart of those pods to clear stuck allocs. Also deploying a hotfix to streaming guardrails (PR #3267) which enforces a 8192 token soft cap and rejects >65536 globally — patch is small but needs rolling restart of streaming-handler. Pushing now.

Ashok (oncall): Please call out customer impact in the page. Jules, update affected customers that we have mitigations and ETA ~10m for routing + restarts.

Jules (support): Messaging: "We've applied emergency routing to protect customers. If you see dropped streams, please retry — we are throttling oversized generation requests. ETA 10m for full recovery."

Sam (sre): Pod restarts initiated at 1794301320. Watch logs for OOMs during drain.

Maria (eng-runtime): Hotfix deployed to streaming handler at 1794301330 (image tag: runtime-stream-guard-1794301330). Rolling restarts in progress (5 of 12 handlers restarted). Change includes: `if request.max_tokens > GLOBAL_MAX { reject 400 "max_tokens exceeds supported limit" }` plus per-step KV cache pre-checks.

Ashok (oncall): Good. Any sign of degraded latency in fallback model? Zoe (product) — FYI for dashboards.

Zoe (product): Seeing a temporary latency bump for affected sessions (+120ms median) but error rate dropping. Good trade. Please capture metrics for postmortem.

ops-bot: Autoscaler scaled decode pool +2 at 1794301355. No further OOM alerts after route change.

Sam (sre): Observed one more OOM on `srv-decode-09` during restart, but it recovered. No new OOMs for last 3m.

Maria (eng-runtime): Verified guardrail rejection logs: a spike of requests rejected for `max_tokens` > 65536 (client errors 400). Example log line:

```
WARN streaming_guard: rejected request user_id=acct_555 max_tokens=100000 reason=exceeds_global_cap
```

Ashok (oncall): Great. Next steps checklist:
- [x] Route large-stream requests to fallback model (Maria)
- [x] Restart OOM pods and cordon bad nodes (Sam)
- [x] Deploy streaming guardrail hotfix (Maria)
- [x] Notify customers (Jules)
- [ ] Postmortem with root cause and mitigation plan (owner: Ashok)

Jules (support): All customer-facing messages sent. No enterprise SLA customers reported impact. Sending follow-up in 30m to confirm.

Zoe (product): Recommend we also adjust SDK defaults to clamp `max_tokens` to a safer default (e.g., 2048) and call this out in the quickstart. Will open a ticket.

Maria (eng-runtime): I'll follow up with a more durable fix to ensure streaming decoder checks tokens at parse-time and adds per-request memory reservations. PR triage after incident.

Sam (sre): Node `srv-decode-09` marked for reprovisioning — it showed memory fragmentation after OOM. Scheduling maintenance window.

Ashok (oncall): We'll leave the route in place until we finish the postmortem and are confident the streaming handler guard is stable. Reopen this thread for handoff to Ashok postmortem owner. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated. Severity: P2 (no enterprise SLA outages). Time opened: 1794301234, mitigated: 1794301460.

Maria (eng-runtime): Quick note for postmortem: root cause: missing token-enforcement in streaming codepath + client sending extreme `max_tokens`. Contributing factor: autoscaler spin-up increased noisy neighbors. Action items: enforce runtime caps, SDK default clamp, add streaming-only per-step mem reservations, improve autoscaler signal to detect OOM thrash.

Ashok (oncall): I'll own the postmortem and schedule a review with runtime and SDK teams. Closing timeline: mitigation complete at 1794301460.

Jules (support): will confirm no follow-up tickets from customers in 1h then mark incident resolved.

ops-bot: Incident channel archived to thread 1794301234 at 1794301465."
